title: Who Counts as Exposed? Measurement Choices in an Open, Re-estimable Index of Occupational AI Exposure
abstract: arXiv:2611.18168v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Occupational AI exposure indices are used as inputs to economic analysis, workforce planning, and policy, and the choices built into them decide which workers are described as exposed. We build an open, re-estimable task-level index and vary its two main design decisions, context and calibration, to show how much the answer depends on them. For each of the 18,796 occupation--task pairs in \onet, seven open-weight reasoning models rate exposure under a common rubric. Each model rates with or without a context of retrieved news and research passages, workplace descriptors, and a bottleneck-based reasoning protocol, and the ensemble is combined with or without simplex-constrained calibration to observed Claude usage. The largest difference from the dominant 2023 benchmark is not a disagreement about what AI can do but about how much credit to give exposure that depends on software integrations not yet built, a choice that no data can settle

translated_title: 谁算作“被暴露”？开放、可重新估计的职业AI暴露度指数中的测量选择
translated_abstract: 职业AI暴露度指数被用作经济分析、劳动力规划和政策制定的输入，而这些指数中内嵌的选择决定了哪些工人被描述为暴露于AI。我们构建了一个开放、可重新估计的任务级指数，并通过改变其两个主要设计决策——上下文和校准——来展示结果在多大程度上取决于这些选择。对于O*NET中的18,796个职业-任务对，七个开放权重的推理模型在统一评分标准下对暴露度进行评估。每个模型分别在有或没有检索到的新闻与研究段落、工作场所描述符以及基于瓶颈的推理协议作为上下文的情况下进行评分，且该集成结果分别在有或没有针对观测到的Claude使用情况的单纯形约束校准下进行组合。与主流的2023年基准相比，最大的差异并不在于对AI能力的分歧，而在于对那些依赖于尚未建成的软件集成的暴露应给予多少权重——这是一个任何数据都无法裁决的选择。
tldr: 本文构建了一个开放、可重新估计的任务级职业AI暴露度指数，通过系统改变上下文与校准等设计决策，揭示了测量方法的选择——尤其是如何评估依赖尚未建成的软件集成的暴露度——在很大程度上决定了哪些工人被判定为暴露于AI。
en_tdlr: This paper builds an open, re-estimable task-level occupational AI exposure index and shows that design choices—context and calibration, especially how to credit exposure depending on unbuilt software integrations—largely determine which workers count as AI-exposed.
